questions.prompt: Board is Ah 7c 2d. How many ace-king combinations remain?

choices.text: 12. One ace is on the board, so the 4 suited AK with that ace are impossible and 12 offsuit-or-other-suit combinations remain from the original 16.

questions.explanation: Four aces existed. One is visible, so each AK combo using that ace is gone. 16 − 4 = 12.

questions.prompt: Pocket pairs are fewer than offsuit broadways because…

choices.text: Pairs use two cards of the same rank, and there are only six suit pairings.
The deck has more ranks than suits.

questions.explanation: Each pocket pair has six combinations. A specific offsuit hand like AKo has twelve.

questions.prompt: If a nit 3-bets and you block aces with an ace in your hand…

choices.text: You reduce the combinations of strong aces they can hold.

questions.explanation: A blocker removes some strong combos. It does not prove a bluff.

questions.prompt: Putting someone on exactly 7h 2c after one limp is…

choices.text: Too narrow. Start with the hands that take the action.

questions.explanation: One exact hand is a guess. A range can be updated.
